title: Proximity Ligation Protocol with Concurrent Immunofluorescence

PART 3: TRANSFECTION Before starting cell transfection: • Warm serum/antibiotic-­‐free DMEM (“SFM” or serum-­‐free medium). • Warm transfection medium (10% FBS DMEM without antibiotics). • Thaw the appropriate constructs by placing in a 50˚C thermomixer with rotation for at least 15 minutes to fully resuspend. • Retrieve the appropriate volume of 1 mg/mL PEI from the Chesebro tower in the -­‐80 and thaw at 50˚ C in the TC room thermomixer. • Prepare pipettemen by wiping their barrels with EtOH and placing them in the hood. Transfection: NOTE: At least 7 hours after plating, cells are ready for transfection. You can start to set up your transfection mixes as early as 5 hours after plating. HOWEVER, remember that you must harvest the lysates between 36-­‐38 hours after transfection for Cos-­‐1 cells, 15-­‐17 hours after for 293Ts. 1. For each construct, label a sterile Eppendorf tube and add 250μL SFM. If transfecting multiple wells with the same construct, make up a master mix, then add 260µL of this to each well. 2. Add the predetermined amount (1-­‐10 μg) of plasmid DNA. 3. Let sit 5 minutes. 4. Add 10 μL thawed PEI from the stock tube; vortex vigorously and spin briefly to collect the droplets. 5. Let this mix stand at room temperature for 15 minutes. 6. Meanwhile, change the medium on your plates to 3 mL of transfection medium using sterile TC pipettes. Bring plates out 1 at a time and put each batch back into the incubator when done. 7. Add the DNA/PEI mix dropwise to the cells using a 1 mL Pipetman, distributing it around the plate. 8. Gently slide plates back and forth and side to side across the incubator surface to mix. 9. Spray the hood with Wescodyne to disinfect and wipe down, then spray with ethanol and wipe down again. 10. The next morning, replace the media with 3.5 mLs new transfection media. PART 4: CELL FIXATION, PERMEABLIZATION, AND BLOCKING Before starting cell fixation:

BUFFERS: To make your own Duolink In Situ Wash Buffer A: Dissolve 8.8 g NaCl, 1.2 g Tris base and 0.5 ml Tween 20 in 800 ml high purity water. Adjust pH to 7.4 using HCl. Add high purity water to 1000 ml (final concentrations 0.01 M Tris, 0.15 M NaCl and 0.05% Tween 20). Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm filter and store at +4 °C. Bring the solutions to room temperature before use. To make your own Duolink In Situ Wash Buffer B: Dissolve 5.84 g NaCl, 4.24 g Tris base and 26.0 g Tris-­‐HCl in 500 ml high purity water. Adjust pH to 7.5 using HCl. Add high purity water to 1000 ml (final concentrations 0.2 M Tris and 0.1 M NaCl). Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm filter and store at +4 °C. Bring the solutions to room temperature before use.

steps.title: Prepare Poly-L-Lysine Coated Chambers
steps.instruction: Prepare poly-L-lysine coated chambers in 6-well plates to prevent cell piling and clumping.

substeps.instruction: Label sterile 18x18mm coverslips (Zeiss, No. 1.5H) with a center letter for condition and a dot in the upper left for orientation.
Cut silicone chambers (Grace Bio-labs) and wipe coverslips with 70% ethanol to remove dust.
Center a silicone chamber on each coverslip and press to seal thoroughly, trimming excess silicone from edges.
Place chambered coverslips silicone-side up into the bottom of 6-well Falcon plates.
Fill each silicone chamber completely with Poly-L-Lysine using a 200µL Pipetman.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 1 hour in a TC incubator.
Aspirate Poly-L-lysine and allow to dry overnight or for several days in the TC hood.

steps.title: Trypsinize and Count Cells
steps.instruction: Harvest cells from culture plates and determine cell density.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate media from 10 mL plates, wash with 5 mL warmed PBS, and aspirate.
Add 1 mL warmed trypsin, distribute by tilting, and incubate at 37°C for 3-4 minutes.
Quench trypsin with 5 mL 10% FBS DMEM + pen/strep; wash several times with the same 5 mL to collect all cells.
Transfer cells to a Falcon tube.
Mix thoroughly and remove a 50 μL aliquot.
Combine 40 μL of cells with 40 μL of trypan blue in a 96-well plate.
Add 10 μL of the 1:1 mix to each channel of a hemocytometer.
Count four 4x4 corners and the center 16x16 square for both sides; calculate cells/mL by dividing the combined total by 5 and multiplying by 10,000.

steps.title: Plate Cells
steps.instruction: Seed cells into the prepared 6-well plates with chambered coverslips.

substeps.instruction: Add media to each plate so the final volume (including cells) is 3.5 mL, ensuring coverslips are submerged without bubbles.
Seed cells per well: 1.5-3 million 293T, 600,000 Cos1, or 500,000 HeLa cells (if using silicone inserts).
If using coverslips without inserts, seed 1.3 million 293T, 300,000 Cos1, or 250,000 HeLa cells.

steps.title: Fix and Permeabilize Cells
steps.instruction: Fix the cells and permeabilize the membranes before blocking.

substeps.instruction: Place PLA plates on ice, aspirate media, and rinse twice with 2mL ice-cold PBS per well.
Add 2mL 4% PFA (pH 7.4) to each well and incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse cells twice with room temperature PBS and aspirate completely.
Add 2mL permeabilization solution (PBS + 0.5% saponin, or 0.3% TritonX for specific antibodies) and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Remove permeabilization solution and wash with 2mL PBS on a rotator (speed 2.5-3.5) for 5 minutes; repeat twice more.
Aspirate PBS and gently use a Q-tip to remove cells from the top of the silicone inserts to prevent well mixing.

steps.title: Block and Incubate Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Block non-specific binding and incubate with primary antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Fill each chamber with PLA blocking solution and incubate in a pre-heated humidity chamber (with 1/2" water) for 30 min at 37°C.
Aspirate blocking solution.
Immediately add 1 drop (~15-20µL) of primary antibody (diluted 1:250 in Duolink antibody diluent) to each chamber.
Incubate in the humidity chamber at 37°C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Incubate PLA Probes
steps.instruction: Apply PLA probes to the target proteins.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate primary antibody and wash twice with 2 mL 1x Wash Buffer A for 5 minutes each on a gentle rocker.

Aspirate wash buffer and immediately add 1 drop (~20µL) of PLA probe solution (diluted 1:5 in antibody diluent; 5µL MINUS + 5µL PLUS + 15µL diluent) to each chamber. For IF-only samples, add antibody diluent.
Incubate in the humidity chamber at 37°C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Ligation
steps.instruction: Perform ligation of the PLA probes.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate probe solution and wash twice with 2 mL 1x Wash Buffer A for 5 minutes each on a gentle rocker.
Prepare 1x Ligation solution: Dilute 5x Ligation stock 1:5 in high purity water (e.g., 5µL stock to 19.375µL water).
Add Ligase to the Ligation solution at a 1:40 dilution (e.g., 0.625µL Ligase to 24.375µL prepared 1x solution) and vortex.
Aspirate wash buffer and immediately add 1 drop (~20µL) of Ligation-Ligase solution to each chamber (or antibody diluent for IF-only).
Incubate in the humidity chamber at 37°C for 30 min.
Wash twice with 2 mL 1x Wash Buffer A for 2 minutes each on a gentle rocker.

steps.title: Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the PLA signal using polymerase.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Amplification solution: Dilute 5x Amplification stock 1:5 in high purity water (e.g., 5µL stock to 19.69µL water).
Add Polymerase to the Amplification solution at a 1:80 dilution (e.g., 0.31µL Polymerase to 24.69µL solution) and mix by pipette.
Aspirate wash buffer and immediately add 1 drop (~20µL) of Amplification-Polymerase solution to each chamber (or secondary antibody for IF-only).
Cover plates with foil to prevent photobleaching and incubate in the humidity chamber at 37°C for 100 min.
Aspirate the Amplification-Polymerase solution.

steps.title: Final Washing and Optional IF
steps.instruction: Perform final washes or additional immunofluorescence staining based on the chosen option.

substeps.instruction: Option 1 (No IF): Wash twice with 3 mL 1x Wash Buffer B (10 min each on rocker), then once with 3 mL 0.01x Wash Buffer B (1 min on rocker). Aspirate and proceed to mounting.

Option 2 (Concurrent IF): Wash twice with 3 mL 1x Wash Buffer B (5 min each on rocker). Aspirate completely and add secondary antibody (e.g., 1:1000) to target chambers and diluent to others. Incubate 15 min at RT under foil. Wash twice with 3 mL 1x Wash Buffer B (10 min each) and once with 3 mL 0.01x Wash Buffer B (1 min). Proceed to mounting.

Option 3 (Sequential IF): Wash twice with 3 mL 1x Wash Buffer B (5 min each on rocker). Add primary antibody (e.g., 1:1000) to target chambers and diluent to others; incubate 30 min at 37°C. Wash twice with 2 mL Wash Buffer A (5 min each). Aspirate completely and add secondary antibody (e.g., 1:1000) to target chambers and diluent to others. Incubate 15 min at RT under foil. Wash twice with 3 mL 1x Wash Buffer B (10 min each) and once with 3 mL 0.01x Wash Buffer B (1 min). Proceed to mounting.

steps.title: Mounting and Storage
steps.instruction: Mount the coverslips onto slides for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Remove chambered coverslips, peel away silicone, and aspirate all wash buffer.
Place coverslips cell-side up on Kimwipes in a light-proof box and dry for 10-15 min.
Place a drop of PLA mounting medium plus DAPI onto the center of the coverslip and invert onto a labeled glass slide (Fisherbrand Superfrost/Plus), pressing to remove bubbles.
Aspirate excess medium and seal the edges with clear quick-dry nail polish.
Store slides face up in a slide box in the dark; cure for 24 hours at RT, then store at -20°C.
Analyze using a fluorescence or confocal microscope (at least 20x objective) after 24 hours.
